claim_judgments.rationale: No supported applicability contrast: both draft and source require the employer to distribute portable fire extinguishers for use by employees on Class A fires so that travel distance to any extinguisher is 75 feet or less. All dimensions align with the text of 29 CFR 1910.157(d)(2).

Concrete contrast: Under the source text of F011 (paragraph (c)(4)), portable fire extinguishers must be maintained in a fully charged and operable condition and kept in designated places at all times except during use. The draft omits the crucial qualification 'except during use' in its summary, meaning the draft would treat an extinguisher being actively used during a fire as a violation of the rule, whereas the source explicitly exempts the period of use. Thus summary is in error.

No supported applicability contrast: both draft and source specify an exemption from paragraph (d) distribution requirements where an employer has an emergency action plan meeting 1910.38 designating certain employees as the only authorized users of available portable fire extinguishers and requiring all other employees in the fire area to immediately evacuate the affected work area upon sounding of the fire alarm.
No supported applicability contrast: both draft and source state that paragraph (d) does not apply to extinguishers provided for employee use on the outside of workplace buildings or structures.

unit_judgments.rationale: No claim covers general scope and application of 1910.157 applying to placement, use, maintenance, and testing of portable fire extinguishers provided for employee use.
C0003 completely and accurately covers the exemption of outside workplace building/structure employee extinguishers from paragraph (d).
No claim covers the exemption/limitation where extinguishers are not intended for employee use and emergency action/fire prevention plans are in place.
No claim covers the complete exemption under paragraph (b)(1) for written fire safety policy requiring total evacuation when extinguishers are not available.
C0002 completely and accurately captures the exemption from paragraph (d) distribution requirements under paragraph (b)(2).
No claim covers the requirement to mount, locate, and identify extinguishers so they are readily accessible without subjecting employees to injury.
No claim covers the requirement that only approved portable fire extinguishers be used.
No claim covers the prohibition against carbon tetrachloride or chlorobromomethane extinguishing agents.
C0001 attempts to cover this requirement but omits the explicit exception 'except during use', narrowing the conditions under which extinguishers may be moved from their designated places.
No claim covers the requirement to remove soldered/riveted shell self-generating acid/foam or inverted cartridge extinguishers from service.
No claim covers paragraph (d)(1) selection and distribution based on anticipated fire classes and hazard size/degree.
C0000 fully captures the 75-foot travel distance requirement for Class A fire extinguishers under paragraph (d)(2).
No claim covers the alternative permission to use standpipe systems or hose stations instead of Class A extinguishers.
No claim covers the 50-foot travel distance distribution requirement for Class B fire extinguishers.
No claim covers the distribution requirement for Class C hazards based on Class A or Class B patterns.
No claim covers the 75-foot travel distance requirement for Class D extinguishing agents.
No claim covers the requirement for Class D extinguishers where combustible metal powders/flakes/shavings are generated at least once every two weeks.
